summary:
All four steps (A, B, C, D) are done in three commits. Verify printed RESULT: ALL PASS on the final commit and git status is clean. Every response body, status and key order is unchanged, and openapi.json is byte for byte the same.

A. Coded errors now go through common/api-errors.ts. I added `codedError` (a general builder) and `forbidden`. `notFound`, `validationFailed` and `conflict` are built on `codedError`. I replaced the hand-built copies in notifications.service, audit.controller, admin-write.service and admin-errors. A new lint rule `coded-error-home` stops a `code: '...'` object inside `new <X>Exception(` outside common/api-errors.ts and ai/. It has two test cases in scripts/lint.test.mjs, and the exceptions are named in scripts/layers.mjs as `codedErrorHomes`.

B. The sign-in limiter is now `auth/sign-in-limiter.ts` with `reserve`, `clear` and `purge`, registered in AuthModule. Its limit and window come from `PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS` in rate-limits.ts, which `PASSWORD_LIMIT` also uses. The three limiter test cases moved verbatim into sign-in-limiter.spec.ts. They run a real AuthService over a real limiter and the fake repository. auth.service.spec.ts now uses a stub limiter.

C. REFERENCES and COUNTED_REFERENCES moved unchanged into `curriculum-admin/references.ts`, which has no Nest or TypeORM imports. admin-errors.ts re-exports them, so existing callers are untouched.

Left out: codes for errors that have none today, and the `AdminErrorDto` rename (both change the contract). I also left ai/sse.ts, the session-lifetime code and the `createdAt` guards alone. No off-limits file was touched, and no docs named anything I moved.

blocking.problem: The new helpers codedError and forbidden decide where `extra` goes: before the message for permission_required and prerequisite_cycle, after it for conflict and importRejected. No test pins that key order. Every existing assertion uses toMatchObject, toEqual on single fields, or body.code. So if before and after were swapped, or forbidden used {after: extra}, every test would still pass, yet the permission_required body would change from statusCode, code, permission, message to statusCode, code, message, permission. The brief treats key order as part of the contract.
blocking.fix: Add src/backend/src/common/api-errors.spec.ts (or extend admin-errors.spec.ts) that asserts the exact JSON.stringify(e.getResponse()) strings, plus getStatus() and the exception class, for: forbidden('permission_required', msg, {permission}), conflict(code, msg, {references}), prerequisiteCycle(['A','B','A']), importRejected(msg, errors), and one helper called with no extra fields.

nonBlocking: api-errors.ts: conflict(code, message, extra) and forbidden(code, message, extra) take the same arguments but put extra in different places (after vs before the message). Name the forbidden parameter for where it goes, or record the difference in a doc; the new spec will pin it either way.
sign-in-limiter.ts:41: purge is public but only reserve() calls it. It could be private, though the brief listed purge as part of the API.
signInAttemptKey stays in auth.service.ts. BAC-4 wanted it in the limiter, but the brief lists only reserve, clear and purge, and the implementer gives an import cycle as the reason. Acceptable.
The 429 text 'try again in a minute' is still a fixed string while the window now comes from PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS.ttl. This was already true before the batch; the risk is drift.
The lint rule matches only `new XException(`. A subclass calling super({code}) outside ai/ is not caught. This is within the brief's scope.
sign-in-limiter.spec.ts drives the limiter through a real AuthService. That is the moved test unchanged, so it is fine, but a later direct limiter test would be cleaner.

Same SQL, same advisory lock, same order, same 429 status and text, same purge batch of 100. PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS equals the old 10 failures in one minute, and PASSWORD_LIMIT keeps its shape.
references.ts is identical to the removed block and imports nothing. admin-errors.ts re-exports REFERENCES and CountedReference, so existing callers are unchanged.
Contract: the diff of openapi.json, migrations and package-lock.json is empty. AdminErrorDto, routes, statuses and codes are unchanged.

Tests: the three limiter cases moved unchanged (same it() and expect() calls, fake repo copied verbatim). The AuthService spec now uses a stub limiter. The lint tests catch the obvious mutations of the new rule.
Ran: 24 unit spec files and 195 tests pass for auth, curriculum-admin, notifications, audit and common; lint.mjs passes; lint.test.mjs passes 43 of 43; tsc --noEmit is clean.

Serialization: in a scratch spec, compared class, status, JSON.stringify(getResponse()) and message for the old and new construction of all 13 error sites and helpers. All are identical, key order included.
Completeness: grep finds no retired name anywhere. The only hand-built envelopes left are in ai/ (allowed) and csv-import.service.ts (no code, file off limits).
Structure: no new edges between folders and no new cycle (depgraph run, imports checked against base).

Repo rules: no comments in the added code, .js import suffixes, no magic numbers, no new dependency. All 3 commits are signed (G) with Conventional subjects. Exactly one new changeset, which is empty.
Scope: no off-limits file touched and no frontend change.
